paragraphs.en: Silver spoke with conviction: "No, not me. Flint was captain; I was quartermaster because of my wooden leg. The same broadside that took my leg also blinded Pew.
paragraphs.zh: 银色坚定地说道：“不，不是我。弗林特是船长；我是由于那条木腿才担任补给官的。正是同一发炮弹夺去了我的腿和普威的眼睛。”

paragraphs.en: A skilled surgeon amputated me—educated and fluent in Latin—but he met a grim fate at Corso Castle. Roberts' men did this, renaming their ships—the Royal Fortune, for instance."
paragraphs.zh: 一位技艺高超的外科医生在我身上施行了截肢手术——他通晓拉丁文，但最终在科尔索要塞遭遇了悲惨的命运。罗伯茨的手下干的这件事，并且他们还给自己的船只重新命名，比如将“皇家幸运”号改名为其他名字。

paragraphs.en: "Ah!" exclaimed the youngest sailor, clearly impressed. "Flint was the best of them all!"
paragraphs.zh: “啊！”最年轻的水手脱口而出，“弗林特是最好的一个！”

paragraphs.en: Silver continued: "Davis was also a man, by accounts. I sailed with England first, then Flint; now I'm on my own. I saved nine hundred pounds from England and two thousand after Flint.
paragraphs.zh: Silver接着说：“戴维斯也是一个男人，据我所知。我先是跟英国出海，后来是与弗林特；现在我自己一个人航行。我在英国攒了九百英镑，在与弗林特合作后又挣了两千镑。”

paragraphs.en: That's not bad for a common seaman—safe in the bank. Saving is key, not just earning. Where are all of England's men now?
paragraphs.zh: 这可不赖，一个普通水手竟能存下钱来。储蓄才是关键，而不仅仅是赚钱。如今英格兰的男人们都去哪儿了？

paragraphs.en: I don't know. And where are Flint's men? Most are here, eager to receive their pay—some even begged before this."
paragraphs.zh: 我不知道。至于弗林特的那些人呢？大多数都在这里，急切地等着领工资——甚至还有几个人在之前主动求过我们。

paragraphs.en: "Well, it isn't much use," said the young sailor.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，也没多大用处。”年轻水手说道。

paragraphs.en: Silver replied sharply: "It's no good for fools—that’s true. But listen: you're young and smart. I see that in your eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 银色尖锐地回答：“傻子才适合那玩意儿——这倒是真的。但听我说：你年轻又聪明，我能从你的眼睛里看出来。”

paragraphs.en: I'll talk to you like a man."
paragraphs.zh: “我会像男人一样和你说话。”

paragraphs.en: I felt a mix of anger and fear when Silver addressed another with the same flattery he used on me. If I could, I would have killed him right then. Meanwhile, Silver continued speaking, unaware that his words were being overheard.
paragraphs.zh: 当我听到银用之前对我同样的奉承之词与他人交谈时，愤怒和恐惧交织在一起。要是当时有机会，我真想当场结果了他。然而，银丝毫没有察觉到自己的话正被人偷听，仍在滔滔不绝地说着。

paragraphs.en: Silver chuckled. "So all your fortune is gone, eh? No face in Bristol for you now."
paragraphs.zh: 赛弗尔轻笑道：“所以你的家当都赔光了是吧？现在布里斯托尔也没你容身之地了。”

paragraphs.en: "Where do you think it is?" Silver asked mockingly.
paragraphs.zh: “你猜猜看在哪儿？”赛弗嘲笑道。

paragraphs.en: "At Bristol, in banks and such," his companion replied.
paragraphs.zh: “在布里斯托尔，就是在银行里或者类似的地方，”同伴回答道。

paragraphs.en: "It was there when we left port," the cook said. "But my old wife has it all now. And the Spy-glass is sold—lease, goodwill, and rigging included; she's coming to meet me."
paragraphs.zh: “我们出港的时候还在那儿，”厨师说道，“但现在我那老太婆全都占有了。而且望远镜也卖了——连同租赁权、商誉和船具一起；她会来接我的。”

paragraphs.en: "Can you trust your wife?" asked the other man.
paragraphs.zh: “你能信任你的妻子吗？”另一个男人问道。

paragraphs.en: "Gentlemen of fortune," Silver replied, "trust little among themselves. But I have a way. If a mate brings a slip on his cable—I mean one who knows me—old John won't be in the same world with him.
paragraphs.zh: “各位商贾，”赛勒里回答道，“彼此之间少有信任。但我自有办法。如果某个同伴带上了我的缆绳——也就是说认识我的人——老约翰就不会再与他同在世上。”

paragraphs.en: Flint's crew was rough; even the devil would fear them."
paragraphs.zh: 弗林特的船员粗野得很，连魔鬼见了也会害怕。

paragraphs.en: "Well now," said the lad, "I didn’t half like it till this talk with you, John. But my hand is on it."
paragraphs.zh: “这么说来，”那小伙子说道，“跟你说了这些，约翰，我倒还真有点舍不得。不过这件事我可认了。”

paragraphs.en: Silver praised me as a brave and clever lad. "A finer figurehead for a gentleman of fortune, I never saw," he declared, shaking my hand so hard that the barrel shook.
paragraphs.zh: 赛勒斯夸我是勇敢机智的好小伙子。“像你这样的船长真是少见，”他宣称，用力握了我的手，连枪托都晃动了起来。

paragraphs.en: By then, I grasped their terms: a "gentleman of fortune" meant nothing more than a common pirate. Silver's words hinted at the corruption of one honest hand, perhaps the last aboard. He whistled for another man, Israel Hands, who joined them.
paragraphs.zh: 到那时，我明白了他们的说法：“有身份的绅士”无非就是个普通的海盗。Silver的话似乎暗示着，这或许就是唯一一个还算正直的手下。他吹了一声口哨，唤来了伊萨克·汉兹，那人随即加入了他们。

paragraphs.en: "Dick's square," said Silver.
paragraphs.zh: “迪克正正经经的,”西尔弗说道。

paragraphs.en: "I know Dick is square," replied Hands. "He’s no fool." He spat out his tobacco and continued, "But listen, Barbecue: how much longer are we to wait like a bumboat?
paragraphs.zh: “我知道迪克是正经人，”Hands回答，“他可不是笨蛋。”他吐出一口烟雾，接着说：“但是听好了，BBQ：我们还要等多久才能不再像摆渡的？”

paragraphs.en: I've had enough of Captain Smollett; he's hazed me long enough! I want into that cabin for their pickles and wines."
paragraphs.zh: 我受够了斯莫莱特船长；他对我已经够严厉的了！我只是想去他们的舱室拿些腌菜和酒。

paragraphs.en: Silver addressed Hands: "Your head isn't much, but your ears are big. You'll berth forward, live hard, speak softly, and stay sober till I give the word."
paragraphs.zh: 银色对Hands说道：“你的脑袋不大，耳朵倒挺大。你得往前靠，过得艰难些，说话轻声细语，保持清醒，直到我发号施令。”

paragraphs.en: "Agreed," grumbled Hands.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”Hand嘟囔道。

paragraphs.en: "When!" Silver exclaimed. "The last moment I can manage—when that's it.
paragraphs.zh: “天哪！”银脱口而出，“我所能争取的最后一刻——不就是现在吗？”

paragraphs.en: We have a first-rate seaman, Captain Smollett, sailing for us. This squire and doctor with a map—we'll find the stuff they seek and help get it aboard. Then we’ll see."
paragraphs.zh: 我们有位一流的水手长斯莫莱特船长为我们航行。这位乡绅和医生带着地图——我们会找到他们寻找的东西，并帮忙把它搬上船。然后我们就行动。”

paragraphs.en: "Seamen are aboard," Dick said.
paragraphs.zh: “水手们都上船了，”迪克说道。

paragraphs.en: Silver nodded, "We'll navigate back halfway before striking."
paragraphs.zh: 银色点了点头，“我们先航行到中途再掉头。”

paragraphs.en: Silver snapped, "We're all forecastle hands here. You can steer, but who sets the course? That’s what you gentlemen argued about—first and last.
paragraphs.zh: 银色脱口而出：“我们都是前甲板的水手。你能掌舵，但航线是谁定的？这才是你们这些先生争论的问题——始终不变的主题。”

paragraphs.en: If I had my way, we’d return to legitimate trade with Captain Smollett. Then there would be no miscalculations and just a spoonful of water daily. But I know your kind.
paragraphs.zh: 如果由我做主，我们会与斯莫莱特船长恢复正当的贸易往来。那样就不会出现误解，每天只需一小勺水就行了。但我了解你们这些人的脾性。

paragraphs.en: We’ll finish this at the island as soon as the treasure is on board. You’re never happy till you’re drunk."
paragraphs.zh: 我们等宝藏上船后就在岛上了结这件事。你总是酒足饭饱才开心。”

paragraphs.en: "Easy all, Long John," cried Israel. "Who’s crossing you?"
paragraphs.zh: “大家别紧张，长腿约翰，”以色列喊道，“是谁在为难你？”

paragraphs.en: "Why, how many tall ships have I seen laid aboard? And how many brisk lads drying in the sun at Execution Dock?" Silver retorted.
paragraphs.zh: “喂，我见过多少艘大帆船被拖上岸？又有多少健壮的小伙子在绞刑码头晒太阳呢？”银牙.za脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: "All for this same hurry and hurry and hurry. You hear me? I’ve seen a thing or two at sea.
paragraphs.zh: “这一切仅仅为了这股急躁和急躁再急躁。你听见了吗？我在海上见过不少世面。”

paragraphs.en: If you just lay your course and a point to windward, you’d ride in carriages. But not you! I know you.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你只是定好航线并朝着迎风方向航行，你就可以乘着马车前进。可你不是这样！我知道你的想法。

paragraphs.en: You’ll have your mouthful of rum tomorrow and go hang."
paragraphs.zh: 你明天会尝到朗姆酒的厉害，到时候可就挂了。

paragraphs.en: "Everyone knew you were a chapling, John," said Israel. "But others could hand and steer as well. They liked a bit of fun, took their fling like jolly companions."
paragraphs.zh: “大家都知道你是个书呆子，约翰，”以色列说道，“不过其他人也能应付得来。他们喜欢寻开心，玩得像是一群快活的朋友。”

paragraphs.en: "So?" Silver asked. "Where are they now?
paragraphs.zh: “那他们现在在哪里？”银问道。

paragraphs.en: Pew was that sort and died a beggar-man. Flint did too, dying of rum in Savannah. Ah, they were a sweet crew!
paragraphs.zh: 佩威就是这样的人，最终潦倒而终。弗林特也是如此，在萨凡纳因酗酒而死。唉，他们真是个有趣的团队！

paragraphs.en: But where are they?"
paragraphs.zh: 但他们去哪儿了？

paragraphs.en: "But," asked Dick, "when we lay them athwart, what do we do with them?"
paragraphs.zh: “但是，”迪克问道，“当我们把它们横放时，该怎么处理呢？”

paragraphs.en: "That’s the man for me!" cried the cook admiringly. "That's business.
paragraphs.zh: “这就是我要找的人！”厨师赞叹道，“真会做生意。”

paragraphs.en: What would you think? Put 'em ashore like maroons? That would be England's way.
paragraphs.zh: 你会怎么想？把他们像流放犯一样送上岸？这可真是英国的作风。

paragraphs.en: Or cut 'em down like pork? That would be Flint's or Billy Bones's."
paragraphs.zh: 要么像处理猪肉一样宰了他们？这可是弗林特或比尔·博内斯的手笔。

paragraphs.en: "Billy was the man for that," said Israel. "'Dead men don't bite,' he says. Well, he’s dead now; and if ever a rough hand came to port, it was Billy."
paragraphs.zh: “比莉最适合干这个活儿，”以色列说道，“他说过：死人不会咬人。”现在他确实死了；而且，如果要说有个粗鲁的家伙来到港口，那非比莉莫属。

paragraphs.en: Silver declared, "Right you are. It's rough and ready, but I'm a gentleman, not just an easy man. Duty is duty.
paragraphs.zh: 银色脱口而出：“你说得对。这虽粗糙简陋，但我是个有责任感的绅士，而不仅仅是随随便便的人。职责就是职责。”

paragraphs.en: I vote for death." He continued, "When I'm in Parliament, I won't have these sea-lawyers barging into my cabin uninvited."
paragraphs.zh: 我赞成极刑。”他接着说，“等我进了议会，就不会让这些海律师未经邀请就闯入我的办公室。

paragraphs.en: The coxswain cried out to John, "You're a man!"
paragraphs.zh: 划船的喊道：“你真是个男子汉！”

paragraphs.en: Silver replied, "Israel will say so when he sees. The only thing I claim is Trelawney. I'll wring his neck with my own hands, Dick!"
paragraphs.zh: 银色回答道：“等以色列看到时自然会这么说。我唯一要的是特拉韦尼，迪克，我会亲手掐住他的脖子！”

paragraphs.en: He paused and then ordered, "Jump up like a good lad and get me an apple to wet my pipe."
paragraphs.zh: 他停顿了一下，然后命令道：“像好孩子一样跳起来，给我拿个苹果润润我的烟嘴。”

paragraphs.en: Terrified, I couldn't move. Hearing Dick rise, someone stopped him, and Hands said, "Stow that! Don’t get sucking of that bilge, John.
paragraphs.zh: 我吓得动弹不得。听到迪克起身，有人阻止了他，汉斯说道：“住手！别胡来，约翰。”

paragraphs.en: Let's have some rum instead."
paragraphs.zh: 我们来喝点朗姆酒吧。

paragraphs.en: Silver instructed, "Dick, trust me. Keep an eye on the keg. Bring up a pannikin when you're done."
paragraphs.zh: 银色吩咐道：“迪克，相信我。盯着那个酒桶别出岔子。你忙完了就端个木碗来。”

paragraphs.en: Dick was gone for a short while. Israel spoke to the cook in his ear, but only a few words were audible: "Not another man of them'll join." This meant there were still loyal men aboard.
paragraphs.zh: 迪克短暂地离开了。以色列在厨师耳边低语了几句，虽然声音不大，但只听清了几个词：“别指望他们中有其他人会加入。”这意味着船上仍然有忠诚的船员。

paragraphs.en: When Dick returned, each man took a drink from the pannikin—some toasted luck, others old Flint, and Silver sang, "Here's to ourselves, hold your luff, plenty of prizes and duff."
paragraphs.zh: 当迪克回来后，每个人从木碗里喝了一口水——有人为运气干杯，有人为老弗林特干杯，而锡尔弗则唱道：“为了我们自己，稳住帆布，奖品多多，还有美味的炖菜。”

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, a brightness appeared in the barrel. Looking up, I saw the moon had risen, silvery on the mizzen-top and shining white on the fore-sail. At that moment, the lookout shouted, "Land ho!"
paragraphs.zh: 突然，桅杆顶端亮了起来。抬头一看，我见月亮已经升起，银光洒在主帆上，前帆则被照得雪白。就在这时，瞭望员喊道：“陆地！”
